source_text: Ac per hoc destruit opinionem peccati naturalis et docet alias esse causas substantiae, alias voluntatis; ac ne intellegentia haec nostro magis imputetur ingenio quam apostolico dogmati, ea, quae huic loco addidit, audiamus: Lex autem subintravit - inquit - ut abundaret delictum, ubi autem abundavit peccatum, superabundavit gratia, ut sicut regnavit peccatum in mortem, ita gratia regnet per iustitiam in vitam aeternam per Iesum Christum, Dominum nostrum [n351] . Assere igitur, quemadmodum peccatum tuum id est traducis coeperit abundare post legem, quae post ministerium Moysi incrementa susceperit.
pass_a_gloss: And through this he destroys the opinion of a natural sin and teaches that there are other causes of substance, others of will; and lest this understanding be imputed more to our talent than to apostolic dogma, let us hear those things which he added to this place: But the law entered under, he says, so that the offense would abound, but where sin abounded, grace superabounded, so that as sin reigned unto death, so grace may reign through justice unto eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Assert therefore how your sin, that is of the tradux, began to abound after the law, what increments it took up after the ministry of Moses.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Consequently, he destroys the theory of natural sin and teaches that the causes of substance and of will are different. Lest this understanding be attributed more to our ingenuity than to apostolic teaching, let us hear what he added to this passage: ‘But the law came in,’ he says, ‘so that the offense might abound. But where sin abounded, grace abounded beyond it, so that, just as sin reigned into death, grace might reign through righteousness into eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord’ (Romans 5:20–21). Maintain, then, how your sin—the sin of inherited transmission—began to abound after the law, and what increase it received after Moses’ ministry.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)
